A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DRIFT and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Visual inspection resolves content omitted by text extraction, including the implementation prompts. Removed and relocated material can be reliably distinguished.

before.justification: V2 reports original AgentDojo and ASB evaluations, component ablations, adaptive-attack experiments, and Qwen policy-tuning results.

after.justification: V3 reports original AgentDojo, ASB, and AgentDyn evaluations, model comparisons, ablations, and adaptive-attack results.

M1.justification: V3 removes the trainable-policy pipeline and Qwen LoRA adaptation described in v2 Section 2.5. It also changes inference: the validator prompt drops History_Conversations from its inputs, and the planner prompt adds an explicit task_thought stage. The three-component architecture remains.

E1.justification: V3 adds AgentDyn's open-ended evaluation data while retaining the six selected open-ended AgentDojo tasks already examined in v2. It removes the ToolBench-derived policy-training data and associated tool-environment construction. AgentDojo and ASB coverage otherwise remains.

E2.justification: The six AgentDojo defense comparators and four ASB defense comparators remain unchanged. AgentDyn uses the same six defenses already compared on AgentDojo. ReAct, CaMeL, and Progent retain their roles in the corresponding model and appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 replaces Claude-3-haiku with Claude-3.5-haiku and drops the fine-tuned Qwen configuration. Adaptive-attack targeting is restricted to the isolator. The retained AgentDojo task counts, utility/ASR metrics, default important_instruction attack, and ASB OPI attack remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The stress-test suite drops validator-only and combined isolator/validator attacks from v2 Table 2; PAIR now targets only the isolator. Component ablations, trajectory-length analysis, the six-task open-ended analysis, the Progent comparison, and the hotel case study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting; removing that checklist does not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: AgentDyn adds DRIFT results of 18.3% benign utility, 20.3% utility under attack, and 3.1% ASR (v3 Figure 5). The corresponding AgentDojo triplet changes from 58.48/47.91/1.29 to 57.29/50.93/1.35 (Table 1). Numerous ablation, adaptive-attack, and appendix values change, while Qwen results disappear. Method and model changes limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The efficiency expression, (Utility − ASR)/Total Tokens, remains unchanged; the expanded security rationale is conceptual.

C1.justification: V3 withdraws the introduction's claims about trainable security policies and offline Qwen improvements, narrowing model generalization to four hosted models. Its advertised empirical validation expands to AgentDyn. The central contribution of combining dynamic policies with memory isolation remains.

C2.justification: V3 develops the argument that dynamic policy enforcement itself creates an attack surface requiring restricted validator inputs. Its AgentDyn discussion acknowledges severe over-defense and a large practical-deployment gap, substantially qualifying v2's optimistic open-ended-task discussion. The generic limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: V3 removes the training-data construction instructions, tool augmentation, two sampling prompts, and tuning details, including 1,000 samples per module, batch size 4, three epochs, and learning rate 2e-5. Runtime prompts are revised. The abstract replaces the direct code-repository link with a project-website link.

R1.justification: V3 adds the AgentDyn citation and removes references supporting Qwen2.5, QA-LoRA, and Adam. Most related-work discussion and comparisons with prior defenses are retained. The introduction places greater emphasis on the attack surface created by dynamic policies.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, Related Works moves from Appendix B to Section 2, and Limitations moves into the main text. The training section and NeurIPS checklist disappear, and appendices are reorganized. The funding acknowledgment is replaced by unfinished template text.

P2.justification: V3 changes typography, margins, headers, and display sizing throughout. It redraws Figure 1, adds the AgentDyn chart, revises the adaptation chart's model groups, shortens the adaptive-attack table, and removes two training-prompt figures. The workflow diagram and case study are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: AgentDyn adds useful evidence about open-ended applicability, and its explicit discussion of poor utility makes deployment limitations clearer than v2's largely positive account. The revised introduction also clarifies the validator's information boundary. These provide a limited overall gain, tempered by the withdrawn trainable/open-model study and inconsistencies between revised Table 1 and the older values retained in Figure 7.
